messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired (PD-INC-7891) — high error rate from load balancer target group 'inference-primary-tg' in us-west-2. Symptoms: TLS handshake failures from edge -> target (handshake_failure / unknown_protocol). Auto-page to #incidents.

pagerduty: Alert details: 500+ failed TLS handshakes in 5m, 60% target_health_unhealthy. Pager: shawn (oncall) -> paged 1m ago.

shawn (oncall): ack. I'm on it. pulling logs now.

maria g.: oncall to triage handoff? I can jump in for infra changes if needed. ETA 10m.

devon (netops): seeing target group health going from 100%->20% around 02:12 UTC. ALB logs show TLS alert "handshake_failure" from backend connections. Not client TLS — backend TLS between ALB and instance.

shawn (oncall): confirm: is this ALB->target TLS or client->ALB? curl to ALB ip fails with "SSL: certificate verify failed" earlier.

devon (netops): ALB->target. Quick check:
```
$ aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:tg/inference-primary-tg
{ "TargetHealthDescriptions": [ {"Id":"i-0abc","State":"unhealthy","Description":"TLS handshake failure"}, ... ] }
```

tara (sre-manager): impact assessment: 30% of inference requests in us-west-2 are failing 502/524 depending on client side. Some customers on dedicated fleets report increased latency.

shawn (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) shift traffic off unhealthy targets to warm pool; 2) check certs on instances; 3) if needed failover to us-east-1 via traffic steering. I'll start (1).

maria g.: I'll verify cert chain. hypothesis: recent rolling deploy may have a package that replaced server TLS config, dropping SNI or using wrong cert chain.

devon (netops): shifting weights to inference-standby-tg now.

incident-bot: action: register-targets called, draining 4 targets, adding 6 standby targets. Change propagated in 18s.

shawn (oncall): quick smoke to ALB after weight shift shows reduced handshake errors but still ~5% errors. Logs show older instance (i-0def) still receiving 20% traffic.

maria g.: i-0def cert expiration: ```openssl s_client -connect i-0def:443 -servername api.redwood.ai``` returns cert CN=old.internal, not matching public cert. So yes, deployment bot rolled bad cert to one ASG.

devon (netops): can we remove i-0def from target group temporarily? If we deregister, ALB will stop sending traffic after draining.

shawn (oncall): deregistering i-0def now.

incident-bot: target deregister request accepted. state->draining.

kevin (eng): re-deploy of service initiated to replace faulty cert. rolling restart of ASG group 'inference-web-2' started.

maria g.: cert fix deployed to i-0def replica; verifying chain now. curl to ALB backend succeeds with 200 and proper cert CN=api.redwood.ai

shawn (oncall): health back to 100% on those targets per describe-target-health. ALB logs show handshake failures drop to baseline.

tara (sre-manager): customer impact summary for postmortem: ~18 minutes of elevated errors (02:12–02:30 UTC). Majority mitigated by shift+drain. Impacted: some POST generation streams truncated. No data exfil.

devon (netops): note: DNS propagation looked slow for traffic steering earlier — attempted CNAME failover to us-east alias but TTL still caused some clients to hit us-west. Changing TTL to 30s for future rollouts saved next failover.

shawn (oncall): are there any outstanding alerts? PagerDuty shows incident resolved; I'll keep monitoring for 30m and then hand to next oncall.

pagerduty: PD status: acknowledged -> resolved by shawn (oncall). Incident auto-closed.

maria g.: leaving followups: 1) lock down deploy bot that pushed old cert; 2) add healthcheck to validate hostname in cert; 3) run canary cert verification in staging. I'll create tasks.

tara (sre-manager): assign followup tickets and schedule blameless postmortem. tagging owners.

shawn (oncall): handing off monitoring to devon for next shift — I'm out in 25m. devon you take lead on any regressions.

devon (netops): taking it. I'll keep watch on 1) target health 2) ALB TLS errors 3) DNS TTL metrics. Ping me if anything pops.

maria g.: thanks everyone. ending here, will file notes.
